children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Prajāpati</s>, he explains the work of agriculture,
for the welfare of farmers, says the seer <s>Parāśara</s>.
A Brahmin who has reached the end of the four Vedas, who expounds the śāstras and is discerning,
even he is seized by misfortune if he is reduced to the humiliation of begging.

children.text: ekayā ca punaḥ kṛṣyā prārthako naiva jāyate
children.translated_text: But by agriculture alone a man does not become a supplicant;
indeed, in this world one possessed of agriculture may become like a king.
Though people may be filled with gold, silver, jewels, and garments,
still they pray to farmers, from hunger for food.

children.text: kaṇṭhe karṇe ca haste ca suvarṇaṃ vidyate yadi
children.translated_text: If gold is present on the neck, ears, and hands,
nevertheless embodied beings may fast when there is no food.
Food is life and strength; food is the accomplisher of every purpose.
Gods, asuras, and human beings all live upon food.

children.text: annaṃ hi dhānyasaṃjātaṃ dhānyaṃ kṛpayā vinā na ca
children.translated_text: Food is produced from grain, and grain does not exist without agriculture;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaṃ parityajya kṛṣiṃ yatnena kārayet ||
children.translated_text: therefore, abandoning everything else, one should carefully carry on agriculture.

children.text: kṛṣir dhainyā kṛṣirmedhyā jantūnāṃ jīvanaṃ kṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: Agriculture is wealth; agriculture is pure; agriculture is the life of living beings.
Even though it is connected with faults such as injury, one is freed by honoring the lunar days.
The whole world has been honored by him by whom a guest has been honored;
by him the gods too have been honored, and he is the best of men.
And thus says <s>Parāśara</s>:

children.text: vṛṣṭimūlā kṛṣiḥ sarvā vṛṣṭimūlaṃ ca jīvanam
children.translated_text: All agriculture has rain as its root, and life too has rain as its root;
therefore at the outset one should carefully undertake knowledge of rainfall.
Therefore, for knowledge of rain, one should examine the king of the year, the minister, the cloud itself,
and also the āḍhaka measure of water.
Now, the determination of the king.

children.text: śākaṃ triguṇitaṃ kṛtvā dviyutaṃ muninā haret
children.translated_text: Multiplying the Śaka year by three, adding two, and dividing by the sage-number seven,
the remaining part is to be known as the king; the fourth from the king is the king's minister.
When the Sun is king there is rain, harsh rain when the lord of night is king;
when Mars is king the rain is always slight, and when Mercury is king the rain is excellent.
When Jupiter is king the rain is good, and when Venus is king the rain is excellent;
when Saturn is king the earth becomes full of dust and without rain.
Eye disease, danger from fever, and every sort of calamity occur,

children.text: mandā vṛṣṭiḥ sadā vāto yatrābde bhāskaro nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with slight rain and constant wind in the year when the Sun is king.

children.text: yasmin saṃvatsare caiva candro rājā bhaved dhruvam
children.translated_text: In the year in which the Moon certainly becomes king,

children.text: kuryāt śasyānvitāṃ pṛthvīṃ nairujyaṃ cāpi mānave ||
children.translated_text: he makes the earth furnished with crops and also health among human beings.
There crop-loss occurs, and disease is constant among people,

children.text: yasmin abde kujo rājā śasyaśūnyā ca medinī ||
children.translated_text: in the year in which Mars is king, and the earth is without crops.
There is health, good movement and commerce, and abundance on the circle of the earth,

children.text: yatrābde candrajo rājā sarvaśasyā ca medinī ||
children.translated_text: in the year in which Mercury is king, and the earth has all crops.
The establishment of dharma, steadiness of mind, and the best cause of rain occur,

children.text: yasmin abde gurū rājā sarvā vasumatī mahī ||
children.translated_text: in the year in which Jupiter is king, over the whole broad earth.
There is always increase for kings and the fruit of wealth, grain, and the like,
when the preceptor of the Daityas, Venus, is king; he makes all crops reach full richness.
War, wind and rain, and the affliction of disease also occur,

children.text: mandā vṛṣṭiḥ sadā vāto nṛpe saṃvatsare śanau ||
children.translated_text: with slight rain and constant wind, when Saturn is king of the year.
Just as the result of rainfall has been stated when a planet is king of the year,
so the result of rainfall should be understood by the learned when it is minister of the year.
Now, the determination of the cloud.
The Śaka year, increased by three, is divided by the Veda-number four;
the remainder should be known as the cloud, beginning with Āvarta in order.

children.text: āvartaṃścaiva saṃvartaḥ puṣkaro droṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: Āvarta, Saṃvarta, Puṣkara, and Droṇa
are declared to be the four rain-clouds, beginning with Āvarta in order.
Āvarta gives water only in one region; Saṃvarta gives water everywhere;

children.text: puṣkare duṣkaraṃ vāri droṇe bahujalā mahī ||
children.translated_text: in Puṣkara water is difficult, while in Droṇa the earth has much water.
Now, the determination of the water-āḍhaka.
One hundred yojanas broad and thirty yojanas high
is said by the sages to be the measure of an āḍhaka.
When the Moon is in Gemini, Aries, Taurus, or Pisces, and the Sun enters Cancer,
they say the water is one hundred āḍhakas; in Sagittarius half; in Virgo and Capricorn eighty.
In Cancer, Aquarius, Scorpio, and Libra, they say the water-āḍhaka is ninety-six;

children.text: anena mānena tu vatsarasya nirūpya nīraṃ kṛṣikarma kāryam ||
children.translated_text: having determined the year's water by this measure, agricultural work should be done.
<s>Vāsava</s> always rains ten parts into the ocean and six parts on the mountain,
and four parts upon the earth.
Now, knowledge of rainfall in Pauṣa.

children.text: sārdhaṃ dinadvayaṃ mānaṃ kṛtvā pauṣādinā budhaḥ
children.translated_text: Taking two and a half days as the measure from the beginning of Pauṣa, a wise man
should calculate the monthly rain or absence of rain according to the sequence of the winds.
There is rain with northern and western winds, and absence of rain with eastern and southern winds;

children.text: nirvāte vṛṣṭihāniḥ syāt saṃkule saṃkulaṃ jalam ||
children.translated_text: when there is no wind there is loss of rain, and when the winds are mixed, the water is mixed.
Each day of the month is reckoned by five daṇḍas;
in the first half the rain is by day, and in the latter half by night.

children.text: dattvā daṇḍe patākāṃ tu vātasyānukrameṇa ca
children.translated_text: Having placed a flag on a staff, according to the sequence of the wind,
the monthly rainfall should be known, making effort day and night.
When, in the month of Pauṣa in the bright fortnight, the sky is whitened by dust and the western quarter is streaked by flashes of lightning,

children.text: pauṣe yadā bhavati māsi site ca pakṣe toyena tatra sakalā plavate dharitrī ||
children.translated_text: then the whole earth in that place overflows with water.

children.text: pauṣe masi yadā vṛṣṭiḥ kujjhaṭirvā yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When in the month of Pauṣa there is rain, or when there is a heavy mist,
then, at the beginning of the seventh month, the earth becomes full of water.

children.text: yadā pauṣe site pakṣe nabho meghāvṛtaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: When in the bright fortnight of Pauṣa the sky is covered with clouds,

children.text: toyāvṛtā dharitrī ca bhavet saṃvatsare tadā ||
children.translated_text: then in that year the earth becomes covered with water.
If <s>Vāsava</s> rains between Pisces and Scorpio,

children.text: tadādau saptame māsi tattithau plavate mahī ||
children.translated_text: then at its beginning, in the seventh month, on that lunar day, the earth floats in water.
Now, knowledge of rainfall in Māgha.
If on the bright seventh of Māgha there is rain, or the sight of clouds,
then the year is rich in grain and gives the fruits of all crops.
On the dark seventh of Māgha, and likewise of Phālguna,
on the bright third in Caitra, and on the first day in Vaiśākha,
if on these there is a violent wind, or lightning and rain,
then the rainy season will be excellent and the earth will be full of crops.

children.text: saptamyāṃ svātiyoge yadi patati jalaṃ māghapakṣe 'ndhakāre vāyurvā caṇḍavegaḥ sajalajaladharo garjito vāsavo vā
children.translated_text: If on the seventh, when there is conjunction with Svāti, water falls in the dark fortnight of Māgha, or if a wind of fierce speed blows, or a cloud full of water thunders as <s>Vāsava</s>,

children.text: vidyunmālākulaṃ vā yadi bhavati nabho naṣṭacandrārkatāraṃ tāvadvarṣanti meṣā dharaṇitalagatā yāvad ā kārtikāntam ||
children.translated_text: or if the sky becomes filled with garlands of lightning, with moon, sun, and stars lost to sight, then the clouds set upon the earth rain until the end of Kārttika.

children.text: māghe māsi nirantaraṃ yadi bhavet prāleyatoyāgamo vātā vānti ca phālgune jaladharaiścitre ca channaṃ nabhaḥ
children.translated_text: If in the month of Māgha there is an uninterrupted coming of frost-water, winds blow in Phālguna, and in Caitra the sky is covered with clouds,

children.text: vaiśākhe karakāḥ patanti satataṃ jyaiṣṭhe pracaṇḍātapāḥ tāvadvarṣati vāsavo ravirasau yāvattulāyāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: if hailstones fall continually in Vaiśākha and there are fierce heats in Jyaiṣṭha, then <s>Vāsava</s> rains until that sun goes into Libra.
Now, knowledge of rainfall in Phālguna.

children.text: pañcamyādiṣu pañcasu kumbhe 'rke yadi bhavati rohiṇīyogāḥ
children.translated_text: If, on the five days beginning with the fifth, when the Sun is in Aquarius, there are conjunctions with Rohiṇī,
there is a fall of water that is very low, low, middling, great, and very great, respectively.
Now, knowledge of rainfall in Caitra.

children.text: pratipadi madhumāse bhānuvāraḥ sitāyāṃ yadi bhavati tadā syāccittalā vṛṣṭirabde
children.translated_text: If on the first day in the month of Madhu, in the bright fortnight, it is Sunday, then there will be scattered rain in the year;
on Monday the whole surface of the earth is flooded by streams of dense rain with unbroken, broad showers.
On Tuesday the rainfall of water is not proper; on the days of Mercury, Jupiter, and the son of Bhṛgu there is joy from the wealth of crops;

children.text: jalanidhirapi śoṣaṃ yāti vāre ca śaurerbhavati khalu dharitrī dhūlijālairadṛśyā ||
children.translated_text: and on the day of Śauri even the ocean dries up, and the earth indeed becomes invisible through masses of dust.
If at the beginning portion of Caitra, under Citrā, the ground becomes scattered with rain,
in the rest it rains little, not excessively, while in the middle of the earth there is much rainfall.
At the beginning of Mūla and at the end of Yama, in Caitra, wind blows day and night;
and the lunar mansions beginning with Ārdrā should be examined for the cause of rain.
Now, knowledge of rainfall in Vaiśākha.

children.text: pravāhayutanadyāṃ tu daṇḍaṃ nyasya jale niśi
children.translated_text: At night, in a river endowed with current, having placed a staff in the water,
on the lunar day of the bright first of Vaiśākha one should determine the rain.
Having consecrated it two hundred times with the mantra, 'Oṃ, success,'

children.text: aṅkayitvā tu taddaṇḍam aṅkatulye jale kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and having marked that staff, one should cast it into water equal to the mark.
Rising quickly in the morning, one should then examine that mark,
whether it is equal, greater, or less, from desire to know the future water.
If it is equal, the water will be as in the previous year, and the flood also will be the same;

children.text: hīne hīnaṃ bhavedvāri bhaved vanyā ca tādṛśī ||
children.translated_text: if it is deficient, the water will be deficient, and the flood will be of that sort;

children.text: aṅkādhikye ca dviguṇā vṛṣṭirvanyā ca jāyate
children.translated_text: and if the mark is exceeded, rain and flood arise twofold.
Thus has been stated by <s>Parāśara</s> the sign of future rainfall.

children.text: sūryodaye viplavato jagatāṃ vipattirmadhyaṃ gate dinakare bahuśasyahāniḥ
children.translated_text: If there is disturbance at sunrise there is misfortune for the worlds; when the day-maker is at midday, much loss of crops;

children.text: astaṃgate dinakare tu tadardhaśasyaṃ aiśvaryabhogamatulaṃ khalu cārdharātre ||
children.translated_text: when the day-maker has set, there is half that crop, but at midnight there is indeed incomparable enjoyment of prosperity.
Having drawn three lines, one should extend them with those same lines;
at all the corners one should place there a three-peaked mountain.
Beginning with the northeast, he should write the southern numbers, starting from the southeast;
by whichever place the goat-transition occurs, by that there will be the result for the rainy season.
There is excessive rain in the ocean, but drought on the mountain;
in the two thickets there is scattered rain, and good rain at the meeting of the banks.
Now, the signs of rainfall in Jyaiṣṭha.
If there is cloudlessness in the month of Jyaiṣṭha under Citrā, Svāti, and Viśākhā,

children.text: tāsveva śrāvaṇe māsi yadi varṣati vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: and in those same lunar mansions in the month of Śrāvaṇa <s>Vāsava</s> rains,
then the year is rich in grain and gives many fruits of crops.
At the beginning of Jyaiṣṭha, in the bright fortnight, in the ten lunar mansions beginning with Ārdrā,

children.text: sajalā nirjalā yānti nirjalāḥ sajalā iva ||
children.translated_text: the watery pass as waterless, and the waterless as if watery.
Now, the sign of āvāha-rainfall.

children.text: āṣāḍhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ surapatikakubho vāti vātaḥ suvṛṣṭiḥ śasyadhvaṃsaṃ prakuryāddahanadiśigato mandavṛṣṭiryamena
children.translated_text: On the full moon of Āṣāḍha, if wind blows from the quarter of the lord of the gods, there is good rain; if it has gone to the fire-quarter it causes destruction of crops; with Yama there is slight rain;

children.text: naikasyāṃ śasyahānirvaruṇadiśi jalaṃ vāyunā vāyukopaḥ kauberyāṃ śasyapūrṇāṃ prathayati niyataṃ medinīṃ śambhunā ca ||
children.translated_text: in the Nairṛta quarter there is crop-loss; in Varuṇa's quarter there is water; with Vāyu there is disturbance from wind; and in Kubera's quarter, and with Śambhu, it surely spreads the earth as full of crops.

children.text: āṣāḍhasya site pakṣe navamyāṃ yadi varṣati
children.translated_text: If on the ninth day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha it rains,
then the god surely rains; if there is drought then, whence would water come?

children.text: śuklāṣāḍhyāṃ navamyāmudayagiritaṭī nirmalatvaṃ prayāti svīyaṃ kāyaṃ vidhatte kharatanukiraṇo maṇḍalākārayogam
children.translated_text: If on the bright ninth of Āṣāḍha the slope of the eastern mountain becomes clear, and the sharp-rayed sun forms his own body into a circular shape,

children.text: jīmūtairveṣṭito 'sau yadi bhavati ravirgamyamāno 'staśaile tāvatparyantameva pragalati jalado yāvadastaṃ tulāyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and if that sun, surrounded by clouds while going to the western mountain, appears, then the cloud pours down until the very time when Libra sets.
Now, the sign of rainfall in Śrāvaṇa.

children.text: rohiṇyāṃ śrāvaṇe māsi yadi varṣati vāsavaḥ
children.translated_text: If in the month of Śrāvaṇa, under Rohiṇī, <s>Vāsava</s> rains,
then rain will continue until <s>Hari</s> rises.
If, when the Sun is in Cancer and in the section of Rohiṇī, rain does not arise,

children.text: tadā parāśaraḥ prāha hā hā lokasya kā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Parāśara</s> said: alas, alas, what fate is there for the world?

children.text: śrāvaṇe māsi rohiṇyāṃ na bhavedvarṣaṇaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: If in the month of Śrāvaṇa, under Rohiṇī, there should be no rainfall,
then the livelihoods of farmers are afflicted by fruitless undertakings.
Now, knowledge of immediate rain.

children.text: jalastho jalahasto vā nikaṭe 'tha jalasya vā
children.translated_text: One who is standing in water, or who has water in his hand, or is near water

children.text: sraṣṭā pṛcchati sṛṣṭyarthaṃ vṛṣṭiḥ saṃjāyate cirāt ||
children.translated_text: The Creator asks for the sake of creation: rain arises after a long time.
And when an ant rises up carrying its egg,
and when a frog makes a sound, then rain will certainly occur.

children.text: biḍālā nakulāḥ sarpā ye cānye vā bileśayāḥ
children.translated_text: Cats, mongooses, snakes, and whatever other creatures live in holes,
and intoxicated locusts run about: immediate rain will certainly occur.
Children make embankments of dust on the road,
and peacocks dance: immediate rain will certainly occur.
If there is pain in the limbs of men whose bodies have been injured by blows and wind,
and if a snake climbs to the top of a tree, that is a sign of immediate rain.
When water birds dry their wings in the sunlight,
and when there is the cry of jhiñjhī insects in the sky, that is a sign of immediate rain.
Now, knowledge of rain from the movement of the planets.
When Mars moves there is rain; with Saturn rain is certain.

children.text: vāripūrṇāṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā paścāt saṃcarate guptaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made the earth full of water, afterward the hidden one moves on.
At the rising and setting of the planets, and likewise at their retrogression and swift motion,

children.text: prāyo varṣanti hi ghanā nṛpāṇāmudyameṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: clouds usually rain, and also at the undertakings of kings.
When Jupiter is in the middle of Citrā, it pours like a broken vessel;
then, reaching Svāti, it releases great clouds.
Svāti alone drives away the clouds heaped up by Puṣya;
Revatī alone releases the rain produced in Śravaṇa.
Now, the signs of drought.

children.text: dhruve ca vaiṣṇave haste mūle śakre caran kujaḥ
children.translated_text: When Mars moves in Dhruva, Vaiṣṇava, Hasta, Mūla, Śakra,
and in the Kṛttikās and Maghās, it immediately causes drought.
The sun following behind Mars would dry up even the ocean;
but the same one, in the opposite position, would flood even the mountains.
Venus standing in the middle of Citrā immediately cuts off the rain;
when Mars is in Leo, then the earth is made of coals.

children.text: sa eva raviṇā yuktaḥ samudramapi śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: The same one, joined with the Sun, would dry up even the ocean.
Now, the inspection of agriculture.
When inspected, it bears gold as fruit; when not inspected, that same agriculture brings misery.
Thus said <s>Parāśara</s>, knower of the ancient lore of agriculture.
And now other sages say:
One should entrust the inner apartments to the father, and the kitchen to the mother;

children.text: goṣu cātmasamaṃ dadyāt svayameva kṛṣiṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: among the cows one should appoint someone equal to oneself, but one should go to the agriculture oneself.
Agriculture, cows, trade, learning, women, and royal households
collapse in a single moment from being left uninspected for a muhūrta.
Agriculture should be undertaken by a capable man, with the desire for the welfare of people;

children.text: asamartho hi kṛṣako bhikṣāṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for an incapable human farmer obtains only begging.
A farmer who benefits cows, goes to the field, knows the proper time, is devoted to seed,
is free from laziness, and is rich in every crop does not sink into ruin.
Now, the rule concerning draught animals.

children.text: kṛṣiṃ ca tādṛśīṃ kuryādyathā vāhānna pīḍayet
children.translated_text: One should conduct agriculture in such a way that one does not torment the draught animals;
grain obtained by tormenting draught animals is condemned in every act.
Though grain obtained by tormenting draught animals may bear fruit fourfold,
it is quickly destroyed by the wind of the draught animals' sighs.
With molasses, barley, smoke-treatments, and also other nourishments,

children.text: vāhāḥ kvacinna sīdanti sāyaṃ prātaśca cāraṇāt ||
children.translated_text: draught animals do not decline anywhere, when they are fed in the evening and morning.
He whose cow-stall is very firm, clean, and free from cow-dung,
his draught animals increase even when deprived of special nourishments.
Where draught animals, their limbs smeared day after day with cow-dung and urine,

children.text: niḥsaranti gavāṃ sthānāt tatra kiṃ poṣaṇādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: go out from the place of the cows, what need is there there for nourishments and the like?

children.text: pañcapadā tu gośālā gavāṃ vṛddhikarī smṛtā
children.translated_text: A five-pada cow-stall is remembered as bringing increase to the cows;

children.text: siṃhagehe kṛtā saiva gonāśaṃ kurute dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: but that same one made in the house of Leo certainly causes destruction of cattle.
Bronze, water in bronze, hot gruel, fish-water,
and the cleaning of cotton in a cow-stall cause the destruction of cattle.
By placing a broom, a pestle, and leftovers in the cow dwelling,
one meets with destruction of cattle; and this is certain from tying goats there.
Where household women dispose of refuse
through the cow-urine drain itself, what lodging for draught animals can there be there?
Even the removal of cow-dung on the days of the Sun, Mars, and Saturn

children.text: na kārayed bhrameṇāpi govṛddhiṃ yadi vāñchati ||
children.translated_text: one should not have done even by mistake, if one desires the increase of cattle.
Avoiding the three days, one should give cow-dung on the other days;
on the days of Saturn, Mars, and the Sun it is remembered as causing harm to cows.

children.text: sandhyāyāṃ tu gavāṃ sthāne dīpo yatra na dīyate
children.translated_text: Where a lamp is not set in the cow's place at twilight,
the herds of cows, seeing that place devoid of <s>Kamalā</s>, cry out.
A plough with eight oxen is prescribed; one with six oxen is practical usage;
one with four oxen belongs to the cruel, and one with two oxen to cow-eaters.
There is always prosperity with ten ploughs, always wealth with five ploughs,

children.text: nityaṃ tu trihale bhaktaṃ nityamekahale ṛṇam ||
children.translated_text: always food with three ploughs, and always debt with one plough.
With two ploughs there is always only the maintenance of oneself;
one will not be capable of giving food to ancestors, gods, and guests.
Now, the account of the cow festival.
One should perform cow worship in Kārtika on the first lunar day of the stick-festival,
tying a dark creeper on the horn and smearing it with oil and turmeric.
Having also made an anointing on the body with saffron and sandalwood,
the cowherds, adorned with ornaments, should raise a stick in the hand.
Then with instruments and songs, having decorated the chief bull with garments and the like,
they should lead it around in the village for the pacification of obstacles to the cows.
Then, on the first day of Kārtika, one should apply to the limbs of the cows

children.text: tailaṃ haridrayā yuktaṃ militvā kṛṣakaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: oil mixed with turmeric, together with the farmers gathered together.
On that day one should have heated iron applied to the limbs of the cows.
and one should have cutting performed on the tail, dewlap, and ears.
By this all breeds of cattle in his house become healthy,
freed from many diseases for one year; there is no doubt.
Now, cattle journeys and entries.
The first three, Dhaniṣṭhā, and those belonging to Indra, Agni, Soma, and Varuṇa:
these always bestow good fortune for the journey and entry of cattle.
On the three Uttaras, on Rohiṇī, on Sinīvālī, and on the fourteenth lunar day,
and on Puṣya, Śravaṇa, Hasta, Citrā, and on eighth lunar days,

children.text: gavāṃ yātrāṃ na kurvīta prasthānaṃ vā praveśanam
children.translated_text: one should not undertake a journey of cattle, nor departure or entry;
his livestock perish, as do any other grass-grazing animals.
On the days of the Sun, Saturn, and Mars, for the journey or entry of cattle,

children.text: gamane govināśaḥ syāt praveśe gṛhiṇo vadhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in going there will be destruction of cattle, and in entry the death of the householder.
Now, the removal of the cow-dung heap.
In Māgha, having worshipped the cow-dung heap with faith,
on an auspicious day and lunar mansion, he should then lift it with hoes.

children.text: raudre saṃśoṣya tat sarvaṃ kṛtvā guṇḍakarūpiṇam
children.translated_text: Having dried all that under the Raudra asterism and made it into the form of lumps,
in Phālguna he should place the manure in pits in each field.
Then, at the time of sowing, he should release the manure;
grain that grows without manure is devoid of fruit.
Now, the account of the plough equipment.
The pole, yoke, plough, post, niryola, its straps,
the aḍḍacalla, the śaula, and the paccanī: these are the eight parts of the plough.
The pole should be five hastas; the post, five vitastis;
the niryola is one and a half hastas, and the yoke is equal to the ears.
The niryola, the straps,
and likewise the aḍḍacalla are both twelve aṅgulas in measure; the śaula is a ratni in measure.
The paccanikā should be made twelve and a half muṣṭis, or else nine muṣṭis;
it should be known as firm, iron-like, and made of bamboo.
The yotra, bound in a circular shape, is fifty-four aṅgulas;
it should be four hastas, and the rope consists of five karas.

children.text: pañcāṅgulyadhiko hasto hasto vā phālakaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: A hasta is five aṅgulas more, or the phālaka is remembered as a hasta;
the kālikā, like the leaf of the arka plant, is nine aṅgulas.
The viddhaka is declared to have twenty-one spikes;
the madikā, nine hastas long, is excellent for all tasks.
This is the plough equipment according to the view of the sage <s>Parāśara</s>;
farmers should make it very firm, for it gives good fortune in all tasks.
Equipment of the vehicle that is weak or not of the proper measure

children.text: vighnaṃ pade pade kuryāt karṣakāle na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will cause an obstacle at every step at ploughing time; there is no doubt.
Now, the extending of the plough.
Under Vāyu's asterism, the Uttaras, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Mūla, and Punarvasu,
and under Puṣya, Śravaṇa, and Hasta, one should perform the extending of the plough.
Farmers should perform the extending of the plough for the increase of grain,
on the days of Venus, the Moon, and Jupiter, especially on the day of the Moon's son.
On the day of Mars and the Sun, and likewise on Saturday,
at the commencement of agricultural work it indicates royal disturbance.
The tenth, eleventh, second, and fifth lunar days,

children.text: trayodaśī tṛtīyā ca saptamī ca śubhāvahā ||
children.translated_text: as well as the thirteenth, third, and seventh, bring good fortune.
On the first lunar day there is loss of grain; on the twelfth, killing and bondage;
the sixth causes many obstacles, and the new-moon day destroys the farmer.
The eighth kills the oxen; the ninth destroys the crop;
the fourth produces insects, and the fourteenth kills the husband.

children.text: vṛṣe mīne ca kanyāyāṃ yugme dhanuṣi vṛścike
children.translated_text: In Taurus, Pisces, Virgo, Gemini, Sagittarius, and Scorpio,
under these auspicious ascendants one should perform the extending of the plough.
With Aries rising it kills cattle; with Cancer there is danger from water-born things;

children.text: siṃhe sarpabhayaṃ caiva kumbhe caurabhayaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: with Leo there is danger from snakes, and with Aquarius danger from thieves.
With Capricorn there will be destruction of grain; with Libra there is doubt about life;
therefore at the beginning of agriculture one should carefully examine the ascendant.
When the sun is auspicious and joined with the moon, wearing a pair of white garments,
having bathed and having worshipped properly with perfumes and flowers,
one should worship the earth together with the planets, and <s>Pṛthu</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: agneḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā bhūri dattvā ca dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: having circumambulated the fire and given abundant priestly gifts,
having fitted the point of the ploughshare with gold and smeared it with honey,
one should perform the extending of the plough in the hollow of the serpent, on the left side.
<s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Parāśara</s> should be remembered;
having worshipped fire, a Brahmin, and the deity, one should perform the extending of the plough.

children.text: kṛṣṇau vṛṣau halaślāghyau raktau vā kṛṣṇalohitau
children.translated_text: Black bulls are praised for the plough, or red ones, or black-and-red ones;
their mouth and flanks should be smeared with fresh butter or with ghee.
Facing north, he should present an arghya with milk,
provided with white flowers and mixed with curds and milk.
'Bring good rain, lord of the gods; accept this arghya, husband of <s>Śacī</s>.'

children.text: niviṣṭo viṣṭare bhaktaḥ saṃsthāpya jānunī kṣitau
children.translated_text: Seated on a seat, devoted, placing his knees on the ground,
the farmer should bow to the god <s>Vāsava</s> with this mantra:

children.text: nirvighnāṃ śasyasampattiṃ kuru deva namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: 'O god, make the prosperity of the crop free from obstacles. Homage to you.'
Then he should offer food and a lamp filled with ghee,
for the prosperity of the crop, to him who is powerful, cloud-bearing, and wind-bearing.
'O <s>Vasudhā</s>, you are golden-wombed and lie upon <s>Śeṣa</s>;

children.text: carācaradhṛte devi dehi me vāñchitaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: O goddess who supports the moving and unmoving, give me the desired fruit.'
An ox with one lame flank should be avoided, as should one with tail and ears cut;
one that is entirely white should also be avoided by farmers in plough work.

children.text: chinnarekhā na kartavyā yathā prāha parāśaraḥ
children.translated_text: A broken furrow-line should not be made, as <s>Parāśara</s> has said.
One, three, and five furrows of the plough are proclaimed.
One furrow brings victory, and the third gives success in one's aim;
but the furrow whose number is five bestows abundant grain.
But if, while the plough is moving forward, it should uproot a tortoise,

children.text: gṛhiṇī mriyate tasya tathā cāgnibhayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: that man's wife dies, and there will also be danger from fire.

children.text: phālotpāṭe ca bhagne ca deśatyāgo bhaveddhruvam
children.translated_text: When the ploughshare is torn up or broken, departure from the country will certainly occur;
or if the plough breaks, the master perishes there.
Or a breaking of the pole may occur, causing the death of the farmer;

children.text: bhrātṛnāśo yuge bhagne śaule ca mriyate sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when the yoke is broken there is loss of a brother, and when the spike is broken a son dies.

children.text: yodhacchede tu rogaḥ syāt sasyahāniśca jāyate
children.translated_text: When the yoke-pin is cut, disease will arise, and loss of grain is produced;
if even the ploughman falls down, distress will arise in the royal residence.
But if, at the time of driving the plough, a single ox falls down,
a human being certainly dies from fever, diarrhea, or disease.

children.text: hale pravāhamāṇe tu vṛṣo dhāvan yadā vrajet
children.translated_text: But when the plough is being driven, if a bull runs away and goes off,
his agriculture is ruined, or else bodily affliction arises.
But if, just as the plough is being driven, a single ox bellows,
and licks its nose, then the crop becomes fourfold.

children.text: hale pravāhamāṇe tu śakṛnmūtraṃ bhaved yadā
children.translated_text: But when the plough is being driven, if dung or urine appears,
there is increase of grain when dung falls; when urine falls, a flood is produced.
The farmer by whom the extension of the plough has not been made in Mṛga and Kumbha,
how can there be any hope of fruit for him in the work of agriculture?

children.text: halaprasāraṇaṃ naiva kṛtvā yaḥ karṣaṇaṃ caret
children.translated_text: He who proceeds to plough without first having made the extension of the plough

children.text: kevalaṃ baladarpeṇa sa karoti kṛṣiṃ vṛthā ||
children.translated_text: practices agriculture in vain, merely through pride in his strength.
In Māgha, earth is equal to gold; in Kumbha it resembles silver;

children.text: caitre tāmrasamā proktā dhānyatulyā tu mādhave ||
children.translated_text: in Caitra it is said to be equal to copper, but in Mādhava it is equal to grain.

children.text: jyaiṣṭhe tu mṛtsamā jñeyā āṣāḍhe kardamānvitā
children.translated_text: In Jyaiṣṭha it should be known as equal to earth, and in Āṣāḍha as mixed with mud;

children.text: niṣphalā karkaṭe caiva halairutpāṭitā tu yā ||
children.translated_text: and that which is ploughed up with ploughs in Karkaṭa is entirely fruitless.
And so says <s>Parāśara</s>:
In winter one ploughs gold; in spring, copper and silver;

children.text: dhānyaṃ nidāghakāle tu dāridryaṃ tu ghanāgame ||
children.translated_text: in the hot season, grain; but in the coming of the clouds, poverty.
Now, the rule for setting aside seed.

children.text: māghe vā phālgune māsi sarvabījāni saṃharet
children.translated_text: In the month of Māgha or Phālguna one should collect all seeds;
one should dry them properly in the sun, and should not set them down below.

children.text: bījasya puṭikāṃ kṛtvā vidhānyaṃ tatra śodhayet
children.translated_text: Having made a seed-packet, one should clean out the grain of different kind there;
seed mixed with other grain is especially destructive of the yield.

children.text: ekarūpaṃ tu yadbījaṃ phalaṃ phalati nirbharam
children.translated_text: Seed that is uniform produces abundant fruit;
therefore one should carefully prepare seed so that it is uniform.

children.text: sudṛḍhaṃ puṭakaṃ kṛtvā tṛṇaṃ chindyād vinirgatam
children.translated_text: Having made a very firm packet, one should cut off grass that has come out;
for if this grass is not cut, the cultivation will be filled with grass.

children.text: na valmīke na gosthāne na prasūtāniketane
children.translated_text: One should not set seed on an anthill, nor in a cow-stall, nor in a lying-in house,
nor in the house of a barren woman.

children.text: nocchiṣṭaṃ sparśayedbījaṃ na ca nārīṃ rajasvalām
children.translated_text: One should not let leftovers touch the seed, nor a menstruating woman,

children.text: na bandhyā garbhiṇī caiva na ca sadyaḥprasūtikā ||
children.translated_text: nor a barren woman, nor a pregnant woman, nor a woman who has just given birth.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ ca takraṃ ca pradīpaṃ lavaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Ghee, oil, buttermilk, a lamp, and likewise salt,
the farmer should not cause to be placed over the seed, even by mistake.
And so says <s>Gārgya</s>:
Seed that has been touched by lamp-fire or smoke, and that has been damaged by rain,
and that has been covered in pits, should always be avoided.

children.text: prothitaṃ miśritaṃ bījaṃ bhrāntyā na nirvapet kvacit
children.translated_text: One should never sow, even by mistake, seed that has been pierced or mixed;
that seed, mixed with other grain and molasses, goes to barrenness.
The farmer, the field's substance, the field, the king, and the gatherings of clouds,

children.text: sarve te vandhyatāṃ yānti bīje vandhyatvam āgate ||
children.translated_text: all these become barren when barrenness has come upon the seed.
This rule has been proclaimed for sesame, rice, and barley;
therefore one should take care with seed, for the splendors of harvest have seed as their root.
Now, the rule for sowing seed.

children.text: vaiśākhe vapanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyaiṣṭhe tu madhyamaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Sowing in Vaiśākha is best; in Jyaiṣṭha it is remembered as middling;
in Āṣāḍha it is said to be inferior, and in Śrāvaṇa, worst of all.
For the sake of transplanting, sowing seeds in Śuci is excellent;
in Śrāvaṇa it is said to be inferior, and in Bhādra, worst of all.
In the three Uttarās, Mūla, Aindra, Maitra, Paitra, Indu, and Dhātṛ,
and in Hastā and Revatī, the sowing of seed is excellent.
In Viṣṇu, Pūrvā, Viśākhā, Yāmya, Raudra, Anila, and Ahi,
having sown seed, a man obtains seed itself.
In sowing and transplanting one should avoid the pair of weekdays;
on Tuesday there is danger from mice, and on Saturday from locusts and insects.

children.text: na vāpayettithau rikte kṣīṇe some viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: One should not sow on an empty lunar date, especially when the moon is waning;
by applying himself properly in this way, one obtains increase of grain.

children.text: jyaiṣṭhānte tridinaṃ sārdham āṣāḍhādau tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: For three and a half days at the end of Jyaiṣṭha, and likewise at the beginning of Āṣāḍha,
a farmer who desires fruit should avoid sowing all crops.
At the end of Vṛṣa and the beginning of Mithuna, the earth is menstruating for three days;

children.text: bījaṃ na vāpayettatra janaḥ pāpād vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: a person should not sow seed there; through sin he perishes.
And so it is said:

children.text: mṛgaśirasi nivṛtte raudrapāde 'mbuvācī bhavati ṛtumatī kṣmā varjayettrīṇyahāni
children.translated_text: When Mṛgaśiras has passed, in the Raudra quarter, the earth becomes Ambuvācī, menstruating; one should avoid three days.

children.text: yadi vapati kṛṣāṇaḥ kṣetramāsādya bījaṃ na bhavati phalabhāgī dāruṇaścātra kālaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If a farmer, having reached the field, sows seed then, he does not receive a share of the fruit, and the time here is terrible.
With mind intent, pure, and with seed sprinkled with cold water,

children.text: indraṃ citte samādhāya svayaṃ muṣṭitrayaṃ vapet ||
children.translated_text: having fixed <s>Indra</s> in his thought, he himself should sow three handfuls.
Having performed the puṇyāha rite for the grain, the farmer, joyful in mind,
facing east and holding a water-pot, should recite the unsurpassed mantra.
O richly blessed earth, giver of abundant grain and fruit,
queen of the gods, reverence be to you, auspicious one, producer of crops.
May all crops grow; may the god rain at the proper time.
May the farmers be well, endowed with prosperity in wealth and grain.

children.text: kṛtvā tu vapanaṃ kṣetre kṛṣakān ghṛtapāyasaiḥ
children.translated_text: But after doing the sowing in the field, having fed the farmers with ghee and milk-rice,
with excellent food, the agriculture becomes free from obstacles.
Now, the giving of the <s>mayikā</s>.

children.text: bījasya vapanaṃ kṛtvā mayikāṃ tatra dāpayet
children.translated_text: After sowing the seed, one should have the <s>mayikā</s> given there.
In its absence, an even birth of the seeds does not occur.
Now, the rule for transplanting.
Sowing and transplanting: seed is of both kinds.
Sowing is free from disease; transplanting is always accompanied by disease.
One should not carry out the drawing of seed for grains when it has taken the form of a tree.

children.text: na phalanti dṛḍhāḥ sarve bījāḥ kedārasaṃsthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All firm seeds situated in the beds do not bear fruit.

children.text: hastāntaraṃ karkaṭe ca siṃhe hastārddhameva ca
children.translated_text: In Cancer the interval is a hand, and in Leo just half a hand;
the transplanting of all crops in Virgo is four fingers.
Now, the rule for tying up grain.

children.text: āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe māsi dhānyam ākaṭṭayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: A wise man should tie up the grain in the months of Āṣāḍha and Śrāvaṇa.

children.text: anākaṭṭaṃ tu yaddhānyaṃ yathā bījaṃ tathaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: Grain that is not tied remains just as it was as seed.
One devoted to farming should tie up grain in Cancer when there is no rain.
In Bhādra there is the attainment of half the fruit; in Āśvina there is no hope of fruit at all.
One should not perform the tying and transplanting of grain on low ground,

children.text: na ca sārapradānaṃ tu tṛṇamātraṃ tu śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: nor should one give manure; one should merely clear away the grass.
Now, the removal of grass from grain.
Even grain that has matured, if it has not been freed from grass,
does not obtain its fruit properly; agriculture becomes exhausted by grass.
Grain that becomes free from grass between Cancer and Bhādra,

children.text: tṛṇairapi tu sampūrṇaṃ taddhānyaṃ dviguṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: though even filled with grasses, becomes twice as much grain.

children.text: dvivāraṃ āśvine māsi kṛtvā dhānyaṃ tu nistṛṇam
children.translated_text: Having made the grain free from grass twice in the month of Āśvina,

children.text: atha pākavihīnaṃ hi dhānyaṃ phalati māṣavat ||
children.translated_text: then grain that is not fully ripened bears fruit like beans.
Therefore, with every effort one should have the cultivation made free from grass.

children.text: nistṛṇā hi kṛṣāṇānāṃ kṛṣiḥ kāmadughā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For cultivation free from grass becomes a wish-granting cow for farmers.
Now, the releasing of water in Bhādra.

children.text: nairujyārthaṃ hi dhānyānāṃ jalaṃ bhādre vimocayet
children.translated_text: For the sake of the health of the grains, one should release the water in Bhādra.
There one should have water-preservation done with water supplied only to the root.
In Bhādra, grain that is filled with water, by various afflictions
oppressed, does not give the farmers the best fruit.
Now, the mantra for destroying the diseases of grain.
Oṃ, success. Reverence to the feet of the venerable guru.

children.text: svasti himagiriśikharaśaṅkhakundendudhavalaśilātaṭāt nandanavanasamāyatanāt parameśvaraparamabhaṭṭārakamahārājādhirājaśrīmadrāmapādā vijayinaḥ samudrataṭe anekaśatasahasravānaragaṇamadhye kharanakharacaraṇordhvalāṃgūlaṃ pavanasutaṃ vātavegaṃ paracakrapramathanaṃ śrīmaddhanūmantam ājñāpayānta kuśalamanyasya amukagotrasya śrīamukasya kṣetrakhaṇḍamadhye vātā bhāmbhā bhāntī śāṅkhīgāndhīpāṇḍaramuṇḍīdhūlīśṛṅgārīkumārīmaḍakādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Hail! From the victorious feet of the supreme lord, supreme sovereign, great king of kings, illustrious <s>Rāma</s>, from the slope of white rock like a conch, jasmine, and moon on the peak of the Himagiri, from a place like the Nandana grove, he commands the glorious <s>Hanūmant</s>, son of the Wind, wind-swift, crusher of hostile armies, with rough nails, feet, and upraised tail, in the midst of many hundreds of thousands of troops of monkeys on the ocean shore: welfare to another, to illustrious so-and-so of such-and-such gotra. In the middle of his field-plot are winds, bhāmbhā, bhāntī, śāṅkhī, gāndhī, pāṇḍaramuṇḍī, dhūlī, śṛṅgārī, kumārī, maḍakā, and the rest,

children.text: ajācaṭakaśukaśūkaramṛgamahiṣavarāhapataṅgādayaśca sarve śasyopaghātino yadi tvadīyavacanena tat kṣetraṃ na tyajanti tadā tān vajralāṃgūlena tāḍayiṣyasīti oṃ āṃ ghāṃ dhīṃ ghūṃ ghaḥ likhitvālaktakenāpi mantraṃ śasyeṣu bandhayet
children.translated_text: and goats, sparrows, parrots, pigs, deer, buffaloes, boars, insects, and the like, all injurers of crops. If at your command they do not abandon that field, then you will strike them with your thunderbolt-tail. Writing the mantra, 'oṃ āṃ ghāṃ dhīṃ ghūṃ ghaḥ,' even with red lac, one should bind it among the crops.

children.text: na vyādhikīṭahiṃsrāṇāṃ bhayaṃ tatra bhavet kvacit ||
children.translated_text: There will never be any fear there from disease, insects, or violent creatures.
Now, the preservation of water.
In Āśvina and Kārtika there is the preservation of water for grain.

children.text: na kṛtaṃ yena mūrkhena tasya kā śasyavāsanā ||
children.translated_text: For the fool by whom it is not done, what longing for crops can there be?
Just as a man seeking lineage protects a woman of good family,
so should one preserve water when the autumn season has arrived.
Now, at the Kārtika saṃkrānti, one should plant a reed in the field,
with its leaves, in the north-eastern corner of the field-bed; the farmer should be pure.
Then with perfumes, garlands, and very pleasing incense,
having worshipped the reed there, he should worship the grain-plants.

children.text: dadhi bhaktaṃ ca naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Curd, cooked rice as an offering, and especially milk-rice,
then one should carefully give, and also palm-seed grain.
The mantra for that purpose:
Children, young ones, old ones, and whatever other grain-plants there are,

children.text: jyeṣṭhā vāpi kaniṣṭhā vā sagadā nirgadāśca ye ||
children.translated_text: whether eldest or youngest, and those diseased or free from disease,
by the command of <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, of <s>Rāghava</s>, and also of <s>Pṛthu</s>,
struck with the reed-staff, may they all have equal flowering.
Having attained equal flowering, may they quickly bear fruit in abundance.
May the farmers be well, furnished with wealth and grain.

children.text: propayitvā nalaṃ kṣetre mantreṇānena ca kramāt
children.translated_text: Having planted the reed in the field in due order with this mantra,

children.text: dhānyavṛddhiṃ parāṃ prāpya nandanti kṛṣakā janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the farming people rejoice, having obtained supreme increase of grain.

children.text: nalaṃ tu ghaṭasaṃkrāntyāṃ kṣetre nāropayanti ye
children.translated_text: But those who do not plant the reed in the field at the jar-saṃkrānti,
their grain species become uneven and barren-flowered.
Now, the taking of handfuls in Mārgaśīrṣa.

children.text: tato mārge tu samprāpte kedāre śubhavāsare
children.translated_text: Then, when Mārgaśīrṣa has arrived, on an auspicious day in the field-bed,
a pure man should make the cutting of the grain, two and a half handfuls.
With perfumes, flowers, offerings, and incense he should worship the grain-plants.
Having worshipped according to rule, one should perform the cutting in the northeast.
Then, placing it on his head, facing forward and with the head held steady,

children.text: spṛṣṭvā na kimapi kvāpi vrajenmaunena mandiram ||
children.translated_text: without touching anything anywhere, he should go silently to the house.
Then, setting his foot on the seventh step, in the chief dwelling,
he should enter and place there, in the eastern part, what has been well worshipped.
One should never undertake the taking of handfuls in the months of Dhata and Pauṣa.
The taking of handfuls in Mārga is best, giving the fruit of wealth and grain.
He who cuts the crop in Mārga without cutting two and a half handfuls first,

children.text: pade pade viphalatā tasya dhānyaṃ kuto gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: for him there is failure at every step; how could there be grain in his house?

children.text: raudre māghe tathā saumye puṣye hastānilottare
children.translated_text: Under Raudra, Māgha, Saumya, Puṣya, Hasta, Anila, and Uttarā,
and on days of Mūla and Śravaṇa, they praise the cutting of grain.

children.text: vyatīpāte ca bhādre ca riktāyāṃ vaidhṛtau tathā
children.translated_text: At Vyatīpāta, in Bhādra, on a Rikta lunar day, and likewise at Vaidhṛti,
and on the weekdays of Mars, Saturn, and Mercury, one should avoid gathering the handfuls.
Now, the setting up of the <s>medhi</s> in Mārga.

children.text: kṛtvā tu khananaṃ mārge samaṃ gomayalepitam
children.translated_text: After making an excavation in Mārga, level and smeared with cow-dung,
the <s>medhi</s> should be carefully set up there on an auspicious day.
Farmers should make the <s>medhi</s>, bearing a feminine name, when the sun is in Scorpio.
By the virtue of the <s>medhi</s>, the farmer obtains increase of the crop.
The banyan, the saptaparṇa, the gambhārī, and likewise the śālmalī,
especially the audumbarī, or any other tree that bears milky sap, may be used.
But in the absence of banyan and the others, a support bearing a feminine name should be made,
furnished with vaijayantī and protected with neem and mustard.
Joined with coriander filaments and furnished with grass and crab-shells,
the <s>medhi</s>, honored with fragrance and flowers, brings happiness from the crop.

children.text: pauṣe medhir na cāropyaḥ krūrāhe śravaṇe tathā
children.translated_text: The <s>medhi</s> should not be set up in Pauṣa, nor on a cruel day, nor under Śravaṇa.
In Mārga it brings increase of the crop; in Pauṣa it brings loss of the crop.
From kapittha, bilva, bamboo, and also from the king of grasses,
men should never make a <s>medhi</s>, if one desires one's own welfare.
Now, the account of the <s>Puṣyayātrā</s> in Pauṣa.

children.text: akhaṇḍite tato dhānye pauṣe māsi śubhe dine
children.translated_text: Then, when the grain is uncut, in the month of Pauṣa on an auspicious day,
people should perform the <s>Puṣyayātrā</s> together near the field.
There, with sweet rice and side dishes, with fish and meat,
and also with excellent meatless dishes furnished with asafoetida and pepper,
with curds and likewise milk, with ghee, milk-rice, and drinks,
with many fruits and roots, and with abundant sweet cakes,
having made that food well presented on plantain leaves with these things,
all the people should feed one another, with the elders going first according to age.
Then, after rinsing the mouth there, with sandal pastes and fourfold perfumes,
they should anoint one another with cooked fragrant oils.
Then they should chew splendid betel scented with camphor and filled with fragrance,
giving it to one another, after putting on new garments.
Having adorned themselves with flowers and ornaments, and having bowed to the lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
they should hold a great festival there with songs, dances, and instruments.
Then all, delighted, should recite a mantra of four verses,
making a hollow with their joined hands and looking at the sun.
In the field, in the uncut grain, by the power of the <s>Puṣyayātrā</s>,
may she, honored by all of us and bestowing good fortune, protect us.

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā ye cāsmākaṃ virodhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who oppose us by deed, mind, or speech,
may all of them come to pacification by the power of the <s>Puṣyayātrā</s>.
Increase of grain, increase of fame, increase of wives and sons,
increase in royal honor, and likewise increase of cows,
increase in the authority of mantras, and increase of wealth day and night,

children.text: asmākamastu satataṃ yāvat pūrṇo na vatsaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: may these be ours constantly until the year is complete.
Then, all rejoicing, they should go to their own homes.

children.text: na bhojanaṃ punaḥ kuryustasmin ahani te janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those people should not eat again on that day.
The delightful <s>Puṣyayātrā</s>, for the welfare of all people,
was formerly performed by <s>Parāśara</s>, accomplishing every aim.
Therefore this <s>Puṣyayātrā</s> should be performed carefully according to rule,
for the pacification of all obstacles and for the increase of the crop.

children.text: puṣyayātrāṃ na kurvanti ye janā dhanagarvitāḥ
children.translated_text: People who, proud of their wealth, do not perform the <s>Puṣyayātrā</s>,
for them there is no pacification of obstacles; how can there be happiness in that year?
Then, in the month of Pauṣa, the wise man should cut the grain.
Having threshed it properly, he should measure it with an <s>āḍhaka</s> measure.
Now, the characteristics of the <s>āḍhaka</s>.
An <s>āḍhaka</s> is said to be a measure of twelve finger-breadths.
Measurement should be done counterclockwise, never clockwise.
Measuring grain by a rightward turn causes expenditure;
by a leftward turn it gives happiness and greatly increases grain.
An <s>āḍhaka</s> made of śleṣmātaka, mango, or punnāga wood is excellent;
one produced from kapittha, parkaṭī, or neem increases poverty.
Now, the storing of grain.
Under Hasta, the three Uttaras, Puṣya, Revatī, and Prajāpati,
under Yama, Mūla, Uttarā, Saumya, Maghā, and Punarvasu,
on the days of Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus, avoiding destructive and cruel times,
with Pisces rising and under an auspicious asterism, the storing of grain is best.

children.text: oṃ dhanadātha sarvalokahitāya dehi me dhanaṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O giver of wealth, for the welfare of all people, give me wealth. Svāhā.

children.text: oṃ navadhuryasahe devi sarvakāmavivardhini kāmarūpiṇi seha me dhanaṃ svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O goddess who withstands the new yoke-load, increaser of all desires, taking any form desired, grant me wealth here. Svāhā.

children.text: likhitvā tu svayaṃ mantraṃ dhānyāgāreṣu nikṣipet
children.translated_text: Having written the mantra himself, he should place it in the granaries.

children.text: samṛddhiṃ ca parāṃ kuryāt tato lakṣmīṃ prapūjayet ||
children.translated_text: And one should bring about supreme prosperity; thereafter one should worship <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Thus the book called <s>Kṛṣiparāśara</s>, composed by the sage <s>Parāśara</s>, is complete.
